sources: Full text: PMC8221129 (J Oral Microbiol 13:1936434), '16S sequencing and bioinformatic analysis'
Primer sequences come from the two papers it cites: Frank et al. 2008 AEM 74:2461 (27F-YM) and Lane et al. 1985 PNAS 82:6955 (519R)

amplicon.paper_statement: the V1-3 region was amplified using the degenerate primers 27FYM [Frank 2008] and 519R [Lane 1985] and the generated amplicons (~520 bp) were purified and tagged with 8-base barcodes; MiSeq, Illumina V3 2 x 300 bp chemistry.
amplicon.primer_evidence: The paper names the primers by citation rather than printing them, so the cited sequences were checked against the reads instead of trusted: forward matches 93-95% of R1 and reverse 97-98% of R2 over 3 runs x 3000 reads (<=2 mismatches, IUPAC expanded). The dominant 5' 10-mer of R1 is AGAGTTTGAT in 94-96% of reads.

insert_length_primer_free.method: measured by R1 vs revcomp(R2) overlap alignment over 2624 read pairs from 5 runs
insert_length_primer_free.note: Consistent with the paper's '~520 bp' amplicon (520 - 20 - 18 = 482 primer-free). V1-V3 length varies more across taxa than V3-V4 does, hence the long left tail.

amplicon.trunc_len_basis: RAW read coordinates, same convention as every other paper here (truncLen applies before trimLeft in dada2::filterAndTrim).

merge_budget.warning: Only 41 bp of slack. V1-V3 on 2 x 300 is marginal by construction: R2 must stay long exactly where its quality is worst. truncLen must therefore be chosen on merge success and retention, not on a quality curve, and a low merge rate here is a real result about the data rather than a parameter to force.

amplicon.read_through: 3.6% of R1 reads hit revcomp(519R) early (median 158 bp). These are short non-specific products, not the main amplicon; they are dropped naturally because they will not merge at the expected length.
amplicon.max_trunc_len_reason: read length; no 3' read-through to avoid

group_assignment.reason: ENA aliases are A1-A63 with no title, isolation_source or attribute that separates case from control. The paper reports 25 children with ASD and 38 neurotypical controls, which sums to the 63 runs, but nothing published maps a given A<n> to a group.
group_assignment.action: This is the paper's blocking issue, NOT its primers. ASV tables may be produced, but the ASD/control contrast cannot be reconstructed, so the paper stays unusable for case/control analysis until the authors supply the key. Do not infer the split from A-number ordering.

not_usable_for: the ASD vs neurotypical contrast, i.e. the paper's entire point: no published key maps A1-A63 to a group

experiment.design: case-control: 25 children with autism spectrum disorder vs 38 neurotypical controls
